svg.title: Failure collection and policy
svg.desc: M1 in progress · committed source baseline. Red cards mark failure boundaries. Collector, observer and final sink have different lifetimes and effects. Reporting an error alone does not choose recovery.
svg.text: m1-968651a · M1 in progress · committed source baseline

a.title: Checked operations return expected. ManagedError retains phase, node, original tree/style/application cause and optional exact text/resource details. ApplicationError keeps the primary phase/cause and separate restoration. Optional independent application and cleanup details do not overwrite the primary managed cause.

Explicit reportError records and notifies, without requesting a frame or stopping the runner. History retains the oldest errors up to maxErrors; overflow increments droppedErrors. Context count and bytes are bounded. Owning diagnostics snapshots remain inspectable after close.

Immediate managed notifications run on UI after recording, before terminal restoration; the diagnostic is borrowed for the call. A throw marks observerFailed without replacing the cause. Nested reports do not recurse; mutation/clear/drain/close are rejected during notification. No managed observer runs after close. The fluent facade can use a fallback observer when no live managed collector can deliver the primary, including a pre-owner setup failure after its cleanup attempt.

Applications may handle a returned checked error and explicitly report it while continuing. Collector inspection or draining does not clear a latched runtime failure. Recovery must respect the operation contract; there is no automatic widget replacement or retry of uncertain output.

Managed runtime failure uses the first-failure path and requests orderly shutdown. Short rejected setup mutations latch their original typed cause before observers and stop later configuration. Callback exceptions translate to boundary errors. Failure of the observer does not turn a fatal result into success.

Cleanup is attempted after failure, including partial construction. Application retains the first phase/cause plus separate terminal restoration; it does not collect every later exception. Managed wrappers retain independent cleanup details and shutdown diagnostics. Resource cleanup does not roll back domain effects. OS and screen restoration have separate limitations; native close has no hard deadline.

The final SceneReport carries a typed final failure or bounded retained/dropped counts after the run/cleanup boundary; full details remain in diagnostics(). The sink borrows the report for its call only. A thrown sink falls back to stderr with the original report. Direct run callers inspect expected and choose reporting.
